lessons.title: Too + adjective + to + V1 (same subject)
lessons.content: 'Too ... to' is used to show undesirable excess. The structure is 'too + adjective + to + V1'. It has a kind of negative meaning — the adjective describes something that prevents the action.

details.explanation: When the same person is both the subject of the adjective and the verb, we use 'too + adjective + to + V1'.
details.example: The girl was too arrogant to listen to my advice.
details.burmese: မိန်းကလေးက ငါ့အကြံ နားမထောင်ဖို့ မန်းကလေး လွန်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'She was very tired' and 'She could not continue working' can be combined into one sentence.
details.example: She was too tired to continue working.
details.burmese: သူမ အလုပ်ဆက်လုပ်ဖို့ အရမ်းပင်ပန်းနေပြီ။

lessons.title: Too + adjective + for someone + to + V1 (different subject)
lessons.content: When the clauses have different subjects, we use a structure with 'for'. The pattern is 'too + adjective + for someone + to + V1'.

details.concept: too + adj + for + person + to + V1
details.explanation: When the person who experiences the adjective is different from the person performing the action, add 'for + person' after the adjective.
details.example: These cars are too expensive for us to buy.

details.concept: too + adj + for + person + to + V1
details.explanation: The structure shows who is affected by the excess.
details.example: Your story is too ridiculous for me to believe.
details.burmese: မင်းပြောပုံက ငါယုံဖို့ ရယ်စရာကောင်းလွန်တယ်။
